title: Variance-Aware Slot Packing for Prefill/Decode to Reduce Padding Waste
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Reduce token-padding overhead and improve throughput by introducing a variance-aware slot packing algorithm that coalesces prefill and decode requests into tightly-packed runtime slots based on sequence-length variance and latency targets.
background: Current request coalescing uses coarse buckets by approximate length ranges. High variance within buckets leads to wasted tokens due to padding, especially on mixed workloads (short prompts + long context). This increases per-token cost and decreases effective throughput on Dedicated pools. Existing efforts (ENG-4721, ENG-62045) focus on bucket shaping; this ticket explores a different axis: slot-level packing with a lightweight scoring function that balances padding waste vs. scheduling latency.
proposed_solution: Implement a slot packing layer in the prefill scheduler that: (1) computes a variance score for pending requests in short windows, (2) forms slots by merging requests with complementary lengths to reduce max-seqlen padding, (3) applies a latency-aware penalty so we don't hold short requests beyond a soft deadline, and (4) exposes a small kernel-selection hint (kernel_score) to the runtime to prefer single-kernel execution when effective sequence-length dispersion is low.
acceptance_criteria: Implemented slot-packing scheduler component behind a feature flag (runtime.slot_packing.enabled)
Integration tests validate correctness: no token duplication/lost KV cache, deterministic slot assignment under same seed
Observed >=10% reduction in median padding tokens per batch on mixed demo workload (short+long), measured on dedicated-gpu-small benchmark
P95 decode latency for short requests increases by <=5% compared to baseline (with flag off)
Kernel-selection hint flows end-to-end to runtime and produces same outputs as baseline when kernel choice differs (sanity test passed)
success_metrics: overall tokens/sec improvement >= 6% on average across benchmarks
p50/p90 latency regressions < 3% for long requests and <5% for short requests
no user-facing error spikes or increased 5xx rate after rollout
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature flagged rollout to internal canary only (redwood-dev cluster) for 72 hours
Phase 1: enable on 5% of hosted traffic + Dedicated low-traffic pool for 1 week, collect metrics
Phase 2: increase to 25% with automatic rollback on threshold breach (error rate or latency SLO violations), run A/B kernel performance measurement
Phase 3: full rollout to eligible Dedicated pools if metrics are green and SOCs approved
technical_notes: Slot packing algorithm: greedy merge with max-slot-size cap and slack budget; compute benefit = sum(max_len_before - new_max_len) - latency_penalty
Latency penalty: exponential function of wait_time/soft_deadline (configurable per route) to avoid long-hold of short requests
Kernel hint: slot produces kernel_score vector {single_kernel_prefer: bool, preferred_block_size: int} written into RequestMeta passed to runtime scheduler
KV cache implications: prefill merges must preserve request->response KV index mapping; we will annotate slots with offsets and validate after decode
Backpressure: if slot formation delays cause queue growth past threshold, fallback to immediate dispatch (disable slot pack) for oldest items
Telemetry: emit slot_metrics (num_requests, max_len, wasted_padding_tokens, wait_time_ms, kernel_score) to Console metrics endpoint
testing_plan: Unit tests for slot merge heuristics (edge cases: single very long request, many tiny requests, equal-length all)
Integration tests with runtime sim that verifies KV indexing and decode correctness
Performance bench: run mixed-synthetic workload (50% short <50 tokens, 50% long 800-1200 tokens) comparing baseline vs slot-packing on dedicated-gpu-small
Chaos test: induce transient load spike to ensure rollback kicks in and no request starvation occurs
A/B experiment runbooks and dashboards: latency buckets, padding token histogram, tokens/sec by model
Security review: ensure kernel_score does not leak sensitive user data (it's derived from length/variance only)
updates: 2026-02-11: Spike complete — implemented a local prototype greedy packer. Observed 12% padding reduction on toy mix. Prototype repo: runtime/packs/proto-2026-02

2026-02-18: Design review with infra and runtime teams. Decided to emit kernel_score as advisory only; runtime final decision based on compatibility matrix. Action: add compatibility check for quantized kernels.

2026-02-25: Integration concerns: KV offset mapping requires small change to packet metadata format. Raised RFC for backwards-compatible field. Punted full rollout until metadata migration tooling is available.
2026-03-01: Feature-flag scaffolding landed on scheduler branch. Added telemetry event slot_metrics and basic dashboard. Next: add latency-aware penalty tuning and run canary tests.
